review_candidates.title: Senior Engineer, Advanced Security Response Team (ASRT)
review_candidates.description: Location: Austin, United States of America Thales people architect identity management and data protection solutions at the heart of digital security. Business and governments rely on us to bring trust to the billions of digital interactions they have with people. Our technologies and services help banks exchange funds, people cross borders, energy become smarter and much more. More than 30,000 organizations already rely on us to verify the identities of people and things, grant access to digital services, analyze vast quantities of information and encrypt data to make the connected world more secure. Position Summary Austin, Hybrid Thales is looking for a Senior Engineer, Advanced Security Response Team (ASRT) , who will work with a team which is dedicated to providing first response to security incidents and focused on the operational aspects of web application security: analyzing threats, suggesting direct methods of remediation and mitigation, and actively working to block attacks in real time. In this customer-facing role, you will continuously interact with customers to mitigate security attacks while creating long lasting relationships through your technical expertise and engagement. Manage technical escalations, and work closely with Product and CS teams for our application security products (Value Added-Services, Dev, Support, Security, Sr. Management) in order to get issues resolved. You will be a technical authority of Imperva’s Application Security suite, while constantly improving best practices for solutions and services. You will work closely with Management to implement and expand the global Advanced Security Response program. Key Areas of Responsibility Serve as a senior technical resource for the Americas Advanced Security Response (ASR) team, providing technical leadership, mentoring engineers, and promoting best practices in incident response and application security. Own the technical resolution of complex customer issues, escalations, and critical incidents, acting as a trusted advisor while ensuring timely communication, root cause analysis, and customer satisfaction. Collaborate with customers, Services Teams, Customer Success, Security Threat Research, Product Management, Product Development, and Engineering teams to resolve high-impact issues and drive product and service improvements. Analyze customer traffic, logs, attack trends, security alerts, and case history to identify risks, recommend security improvements, and strengthen customers' overall application security posture. Design, implement, and optimize custom security policies that detect, prevent, and mitigate application-layer attacks while minimizing false positives and ensuring optimal application availability. Serve as technical escalation point during sophisticated application attacks, including large-scale Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) incidents, zero-day threats, and advanced web application exploits. Perform forensic analysis of application logs, security events, and attack payloads to identify vulnerabilities, validate attack patterns, and provide actionable remediation recommendations. Document technical findings, create knowledge base articles, and share best practices that improve operational consistency, accelerate incident resolution, and enhance the technical capabilities of the ASR team. Develop and maintain automation solutions to streamline ASR workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve incident response efficiency. Minimum Qualifications Minimum of 4 year bachelors degree in Information Systems or Computer Science or Telecommunications or any Technology field and minimum of 6 years experience in application or network security in a customer facing role with at least last 3 years in Security Engineering/Threat Mitigation role OR 4 years’ experience in application or network security with a Master’s degree in a technology field with at least 2 years in Security Engineering/Threat mitigation role. Excellent analytical and problem-solving approach alongside self-learning ability. Passion for customer success/advocacy. Demonstrated experience in working with Internet Security and Networking Technologies such as TCP/IP, HTTP, SSL/TLS, Proxies, Firewalls, OWASP Top 10, and OWASP Automated Threats to Web Applications. Hands-on experience in identifying BOT behaviors and mitigating BOT attacks. And with web application vulnerabilities and common attack techniques (SQLi, XSS, OWASP Top 10, etc). Experience with one or more scripting languages (i.e. python, bash, java, etc). Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer at the time of hire. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship or for assuming sponsorship of an employment visa now or in the future. Preferred Qualifications Expertise with network security architecture, engineering, and security frameworks. Ability to anticipate customer and team expectations/needs and communicate effectively with relevant teams to resolve technical issues. A degree of flexibility to take appointments evenings and mornings, as required. Bilingual (English and Spanish or Portuguese) working/professional proficiency Why Join Us? Say HI and learn more about working at Thales click here . This position will require successfully completing a post-offer background check. Qualified candidates with [a] criminal history will be considered and are not automatically disqualified, consistent with federal law, state law, and local ordinances. Thales champions inclusion and we believe diversity strengthens the fabric of our culture. Thales is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability/veterans. If you need an accommodation or assistance in order to apply for a position with Thales, please contact us at talentacquisition@us.thalesgroup.com. The reference Total Target Compensation (TTC) market range for this position, inclusive of annual base salary and the variable compensation target, is between Total Target Cash (TTC) 93,192.00 - 155,775.00 USD Annual This reflects how companies in a similar industry and geographic region generally pay for similar jobs. This range helps the Company make pay decisions as one data point among many. Where a position falls within this range is also dependent on other factors including – but not limited to – the employee’s career path history, competencies, skills and performance, as well as the company’s annual salary budget, the customer’s program requirements, and the company’s internal equity. Thales may offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s status protected by local, state, or federal law. (For Internal candidate, if you need more information, please raise HR request through MyThales) Thales provides an extensive benefits program for all full-time employees working 30 or more hours per week and their eligible dependents, including the following: Elective Health, Dental, Vision, FSA/HSA, Voluntary Life and AD&D, Whole Group Life w/LTC, Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity, Accident Insurance, Legal Plan, Identity Theft, and Pet Insurance Retirement Savings Plan after 30 days of employment with a company contribution and a match, and with no vesting period Company paid holidays and Paid Time Off Company provided Life Insurance, AD&D, Disability, Employee Assistance Plan, and Well-being Program

review_candidates.description: Description Lighthouse Works is a mission-driven, values-based organization that creates competitive, integrated employment opportunities for working-age individuals who are blind or visually impaired in Central Florida. We also deliver business services that support and expand rehabilitation training at Lighthouse Central Florida. Position Summary Lighthouse Works is seeking an IT Support Technician to provide full-time, on-site technology support at an assigned Neighborhood Schools Initiative (NSI) school in Orlando, FL. This position serves as the primary technology support contact for faculty, staff, and students, resolving day-to-day technical issues, maintaining devices and classroom technology, and coordinating advanced support with the Lighthouse IT team and school district partners. Essential Responsibilities Provide responsive, customer-focused Tier 1 and Tier 2 technical support for hardware, software, user accounts, printers, wireless connectivity, classroom technology, and communication systems. Manage support requests through the designated ticketing system, documenting troubleshooting, prioritizing issues, communicating updates, and ensuring timely resolution or escalation. Install, configure, deploy, maintain, and troubleshoot computers, Chromebooks, tablets, printers, interactive displays, projectors, and other technology equipment. Support Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, educational applications, user onboarding and offboarding, account access, and password resets within authorized procedures. Perform routine maintenance, software updates, security patching, device inspections, and equipment inventory management. Coordinate escalated technical issues with the Lighthouse IT team, Orange County Public Schools (OCPS), and approved vendors. Assist with technology deployments, system changes, classroom presentations, school events, and student assessments. Maintain accurate asset records, technical documentation, user guides, and support procedures; provide basic technology training to users. Identify and promptly report cybersecurity concerns, equipment loss, unauthorized access, and potential exposure of confidential information. Protect student, employee, organizational, and client information while following established security, confidentiality, and access-control requirements. Collaborate with school leadership, Lighthouse colleagues, district staff, and vendors to resolve issues and improve technology services. Demonstrate Lighthouse’s Core Values of Servant Leadership, Inclusion, Collaboration, Empowerment, and Excellence. Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications Education Associate’s degree in IT or a related field, or equivalent education, technical training, and relevant experience required. Bachelor’s degree preferred. Experience Three or more years of hands-on IT, desktop, or help desk support experience required. Experience supporting Windows, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, printers, mobile devices, and audiovisual technology. Familiarity with ticketing systems, remote support tools, user account administration, device deployment, and asset tracking. K–12 school technology support and experience working with a school district or managed service provider preferred. Knowledge And Skills Strong troubleshooting skills and working knowledge of TCP/IP, LAN/WAN connectivity, wireless networks, device management, endpoint security, and preventive maintenance. Excellent customer service and communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to nontechnical users. Ability to prioritize competing requests, document work accurately, work independently, and recognize when escalation is needed. Sound judgment, discretion with confidential information, adaptability, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including assistive technology. Certifications Technical certifications are preferred but not required. Examples include CompTIA A+, CompTIA Network+, and relevant Microsoft or Google certifications. Physical Requirements Regular computer use, walking, and standing throughout the school campus. Ability to move and handle equipment weighing up to 50 pounds, with appropriate assistance or equipment as needed. Occasional bending, kneeling, reaching, and use of a step ladder. Reasonable accommodations may be available to enable individuals to perform essential functions. Additional Requirements Work full-time on-site at the assigned school during the established schedule, with reliable attendance and transportation. Successfully complete a Level II background screening and meet applicable school and client access requirements. Maintain confidentiality and comply with Lighthouse policies, school safety procedures, and client security requirements. Work occasional approved evenings or weekends for school events, technology deployments, maintenance, or urgent support. Travel to Lighthouse or other client locations as needed and coordinated with school coverage. Participate in ongoing technical training and professional development. Qualifications Education: Associate’s degree in information technology or a related field, or equivalent education, technical training, and relevant experience required. Bachelor’s degree preferred. License And Certification: Technical certifications are preferred, not required. Examples include CompTIA A+, CompTIA Network+, and relevant Microsoft or Google credentials. Demonstrated experience and work performance are the primary considerations. Experience: Three or more years of hands-on IT, desktop, or help desk support experience required. Experience supporting Windows, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, printers, mobile devices, and classroom or audiovisual technology. Experience with ticketing systems, remote support, user account administration, device deployment, and asset tracking. K–12 or charter school experience preferred. Experience working with an MSP, OCPS, or another school district preferred. Demonstrated Knowledge And Skills: Strong troubleshooting skills across computer hardware, operating systems, applications, peripherals, and communications equipment. Working knowledge of TCP/IP, LAN and WAN connectivity, wireless networks, and basic network troubleshooting. Knowledge of account permissions, device imaging and management, software licensing, patching, endpoint security, and preventive maintenance. Excellent customer service and communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical users and provide patient guidance. Ability to prioritize competing requests, organize work, document accurately, and follow issues through to resolution. Ability to work independently, recognize when escalation is needed, and collaborate with school staff, Lighthouse colleagues, and vendors. Sound judgment and discretion with sensitive information; ability to remain professional under pressure and adapt to changing systems and responsibilities. Ability to learn new technologies and support users with diverse needs, including users of assistive technology. Physical Demands: Frequent computer use and communication with users; regular walking and standing throughout a school campus. Move, install, and handle technology equipment, at times weighing up to 50 pounds, using appropriate assistance or equipment as needed. Bending, kneeling, reaching, and occasional use of a step ladder to access equipment. Essential functions may be performed with reasonable accommodations. Requirements: Work on-site at the assigned school full time during the established schedule; maintain reliable attendance and transportation. Pass a Level II background screening and meet applicable school and client access requirements. Maintain confidentiality and comply with Lighthouse policies, school safety procedures, and applicable client security requirements. Work occasional approved evenings or weekends for school events, deployments, maintenance, or urgent support. Travel to Lighthouse or other client locations as assigned and coordinated with school coverage. Participate in ongoing technical training and professional development.
